_meta.purpose: Realistic personal health facts for synthetic GB respondents. No data from More in Common's June 2023 poll for 11 London is used.
_meta.conventions: Percentages, 1 d.p. where the source gives it. Age bands exactly as published. by_age = persons; by_age_sex given where the source splits by sex (census sources publish no persons column by age).

facts.measure: At least one longstanding illness or condition. HSE question (ONS harmonised, since 2012): 'Do you have any physical or mental health conditions or illnesses lasting or expected to last 12 months or more?'
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ living in private households
facts.source: NHS England, Health Survey for England 2022 Part 2: Adults' health (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 1: General health, longstanding illness and acute sickness, by survey year and sex (row 'At least one longstanding illness', column 2022)
facts.notes: Report page: https://digital.nhs.uk/data-and-information/publications/statistical/health-survey-for-england/2022-part-2/adult-health ('In 2022, 41% of adults had at least one longstanding illness or condition'). HSE 2022 tables publish no age breakdown of longstanding illness; use census_any_condition / disabled_equality_act below for the age gradient. Most common condition groups 2022 (Table 2): musculoskeletal 14%, mental/behavioural/neurodevelopmental 11%, heart & circulatory 9%, diabetes/endocrine/metabolic 8%, respiratory 7%. Survey self-report gives a much higher figure than the census (41% v ~24% of all ages); the two measures are not interchangeable.

facts.measure: Has a physical or mental health condition or illness lasting or expected to last 12 months or more (disabled limited a lot + limited a little + non-disabled with non-limiting condition). Census question: 'Do you have any physical or mental health conditions or illnesses lasting or expected to last 12 months or more?'
facts.source: ONS, Disability by age, sex and deprivation, England and Wales: Census 2021 (released 8 February 2023)
facts.table: Figure 1 data download (https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/dvc2232/fig1/datadownload.xlsx): Age-specific percentages of disability by age group and sex, England 2021
facts.notes: Derived as 100 minus the published 'Non-disabled; no condition' age-specific percentage. Published only by sex within age (no persons column). Census self-report of conditions is markedly lower than HSE's 41% longstanding illness; census was taken during COVID-19 restrictions and the 2021 question dropped the 'problems related to old age' prompt, which ONS says may have lowered older-age figures.

facts.measure: Disabled under the Equality Act 2010 definition: has a long-term physical or mental health condition that reduces ability to carry out day-to-day activities a little or a lot ('Do any of your conditions or illnesses reduce your ability to carry out day-to-day activities?' = 'Yes, a lot' or 'Yes, a little')
facts.source: ONS, Disability by age, sex and deprivation, England and Wales: Census 2021 (released 8 February 2023)
facts.table: Figure 1 data download (dvc2232/fig1/datadownload.xlsx); 'limited a lot' + 'limited a little' summed per age and sex
facts.notes: Overall: 'In England, 18.7% of females and 16.5% of males were disabled'; 17.7% of people in England (Disability Topic Summary, as quoted in the article; age-standardised). Wales: 22.3% females, 19.8% males. Age-specific values are the sum of the two published 'limited' categories (rounding may make them differ by 0.1 from ONS text, e.g. ONS text gives females 20-24 as 15.1% vs 15.2% summed).

facts.measure: Took at least one prescribed medicine in the last week (excluding contraceptives and smoking-cessation products / nicotine replacement), recorded at the HSE nurse visit
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ in private households
facts.source: NHS Digital, Health Survey for England 2016: Prescribed medicines (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 1: Number of prescribed medicines taken in the last week, by age and sex
facts.notes: Report: https://files.digital.nhs.uk/pdf/3/c/hse2016-pres-med.pdf (Key findings: 'In 2015/16 48% of adults had taken at least one prescribed medicine ... increased with age from 19% of young adults aged 16 to 24 to more than 90% of those aged 75 and over'; '24% of adults were taking three or more medicines'). Data pool HSE 2015 and 2016. Base: aged 16+ with a nurse visit, private households (care homes excluded). Report rounds 16-24 'at least one' to 19%; table value 18.6%.

facts.measure: Took three or more prescribed medicines in the last week (same definition)
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ in private households
facts.source: NHS Digital, Health Survey for England 2016: Prescribed medicines (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 1: Number of prescribed medicines taken in the last week, by age and sex
facts.notes: Report: https://files.digital.nhs.uk/pdf/3/c/hse2016-pres-med.pdf (Key findings: 'In 2015/16 48% of adults had taken at least one prescribed medicine ... increased with age from 19% of young adults aged 16 to 24 to more than 90% of those aged 75 and over'; '24% of adults were taking three or more medicines'). Data pool HSE 2015 and 2016. Base: aged 16+ with a nurse visit, private households (care homes excluded). Report rounds 16-24 'at least one' to 19%; table value 18.6%.

facts.measure: Took five or more prescribed medicines in the last week (same definition)
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ in private households
facts.source: NHS Digital, Health Survey for England 2016: Prescribed medicines (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 1: Number of prescribed medicines taken in the last week, by age and sex
facts.notes: Report: https://files.digital.nhs.uk/pdf/3/c/hse2016-pres-med.pdf (Key findings: 'In 2015/16 48% of adults had taken at least one prescribed medicine ... increased with age from 19% of young adults aged 16 to 24 to more than 90% of those aged 75 and over'; '24% of adults were taking three or more medicines'). Data pool HSE 2015 and 2016. Base: aged 16+ with a nurse visit, private households (care homes excluded). Report rounds 16-24 'at least one' to 19%; table value 18.6%. 5+ derived by summing Table 1 rows '5','6','7','8 or more' (report text confirms: 'from 9% of those aged 45 to 54 to 56% of those aged 85 and over').

facts.measure: 'It is thought that between a third and a half of all medicines prescribed for long-term conditions are not taken as recommended.'
facts.geography: UK (NICE guideline for England; evidence-based estimate, not a survey of people)
facts.source: NICE, Medicines adherence: involving patients in decisions about prescribed medicines and supporting adherence (CG76), Introduction
facts.notes: This is a share of MEDICINES (prescriptions), not of PEOPLE. No official or peer-reviewed nationally representative UK survey of the share of adults who have ever skipped/stopped a prescribed medicine was found; only commercial polls (e.g. ComRes for Omnicell 2015: 21% missed a daily dose, 12% did not finish a course) which were not opened/verified and are not official or peer-reviewed, so are excluded.

facts.measure: Provides unpaid care. Census question: 'Do you look after, or give any help or support to, anyone because they have long-term physical or mental health conditions or illnesses, or problems related to old age?' (excluding anything done as part of paid employment)
facts.source: ONS, Unpaid care by age, sex and deprivation, England and Wales: Census 2021 (released 13 February 2023)
facts.table: Figure 1 data download (https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/dvc2234/fig1/datadownload.xlsx): Age-specific percentages of unpaid carers by age group, sex and number of unpaid care hours provided per week, England, 2021
facts.notes: Age-specific values = sum of the five published weekly-hours bands (9h or less; 10-19; 20-34; 35-49; 50+) per age and sex; they reproduce ONS text peaks (females 55-59 19.9%, males 60-64 13.0%). Overall 8.9% is the age-standardised % of usual residents aged 5+ in England (Wales 10.5%). Hours split per age is available in the same file if needed (e.g. 50+ hours rises to ~5% of women 65+).

facts.measure: Below the competency threshold needed to understand and use commonly used English health information materials: (a) text (literacy) only; (b) text + numeracy
facts.year: Skills data: 2011 Skills for Life Survey (fieldwork May 2010 - Feb 2011); paper published 2015
facts.source: Rowlands G, Protheroe J, Winkley J, Richardson M, Seed PT, Rudd R. A mismatch between population health literacy and the complexity of health information: an observational study. British Journal of General Practice 2015;65(635):e379-e386. doi:10.3399/bjgp15X685285
facts.table: Results / Abstract; Table 2 'Literacy competency descriptive analyses'
facts.notes: Abstract: '2515/5795 participants (43%) were below the text-only threshold, while 2905/4767 (61%) were below the text + numeracy threshold.' by_age and by_sex are TEXT-ONLY. by_age computed from Table 2 counts (16-44: 1439/3500; 45-65: 1074/2292) because the printed percentages in that table (57% and 43%) do not match their own counts; the paper's text says older people (45-65) had higher odds of being below threshold, consistent with the counts. No age split published for text + numeracy. Survey excluded adults over 65.

facts.measure: '1 in 17 people being affected by a rare disease at some point in their lifetime' ('In the UK this amounts to over 3.5 million people'); rare disease = 'a condition which affects less than 1 in 2,000 people'
facts.source: Department of Health and Social Care, The UK Rare Diseases Framework
facts.notes: overall = 1/17 as a percentage (lifetime). This is prevalence, not public awareness; no official or peer-reviewed survey of UK public awareness of rare diseases was found (see not_found).

facts.measure: 'Only 14% of people have ever taken part in a clinical trial, despite 85% saying they want to help the NHS find better treatments'
facts.source: NIHR press release 'Public urged to take part in clinical research to find new NHS treatments' (NIHR CLAHRC/ARC West archive)
facts.notes: WEAK SOURCE: an NIHR (official body) press release reporting a commissioned poll; pollster, fieldwork dates and question wording are not stated, and it is not peer-reviewed. Use as indicative only.

facts.measure: Any common mental health condition (CMHC) in the past week, identified by the Clinical Interview Schedule - Revised (CIS-R): generalised anxiety disorder, depression, phobias, OCD, panic disorder, or CMHC not otherwise specified
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ living in private households
facts.source: NHS England, Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey: Survey of Mental Health and Wellbeing, England, 2023/4 - Chapter 1: Common mental health conditions
facts.table: Key findings / chapter text; chart 'Prevalence of common mental health conditions (CMHCs) in past week, by gender (Base: All adults)'
facts.notes: Only these age bands are stated numerically for 'any CMHC' (Figure 1.8 by age is published as an image only, so other bands are not transcribed). 16-64 by sex: men 17.3%, women 27.8%. For a full age gradient use cisr_12plus below (closely related measure). Specific conditions by age and sex (GAD, depression etc.) are in the chapter chart downloads.

facts.measure: CIS-R score of 12 or more (CMHC symptoms 'of a level likely to benefit from acknowledgement and possible intervention'); 18+ = severe symptoms
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ in private households
facts.source: NHS England, APMS 2023/4, Chapter 1: Common mental health conditions
facts.table: Chart data 'CIS-R score of 12-17 and 18 or more, by age (Base: All adults)'
facts.notes: by_age = published 12-17 share + published 18+ share (disjoint categories). Text confirms 22.8% of 16-24s and 9.4% of 75+. Severe (18+): overall 10.0%, men 7.5%, women 11.9%.

facts.measure: GHQ-12 score of 4 or more ('indicating probable psychological disturbance or mental ill health')
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ in private households
facts.source: NHS England, Health Survey for England 2022 Part 2: Adults' health (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 3: Prevalence of mental ill health according to GHQ-12, by age and sex
facts.notes: Alternative self-completion screening measure to APMS; values are from the table as published (1 d.p.).

facts.measure: Current cigarette smoker: 'Have you ever smoked cigarettes regularly?' -> 'Do you smoke cigarettes at all nowadays?' = yes (Annual Population Survey)
facts.geography: UK, adults aged 18+ (by-age figures UK; England overall 9.5%)
facts.source: ONS, Adult smoking habits in the UK: 2025
facts.table: Figure 3 data download (https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/dvc3642/fig03/datadownload.xlsx): Percentage who were current smokers, all persons by age group, UK, 2011 to 2025
facts.notes: UK overall 9.8%; England 9.5%, Wales 11.1%, Scotland 11.4%, NI 9.9%. Wording of the two APS questions taken from the 2024 edition of the same bulletin. E-cigarette use (OPN, GB, 16+, 2025): 9.9% daily or occasional, highest at 25-34 (16.4%).

facts.measure: Obese: measured BMI of 30 kg/m2 or more (includes morbidly obese, BMI 40+)
facts.geography: England, adults aged 16+ with valid height and weight measurements
facts.source: NHS England, Health Survey for England 2022 Part 2: Overweight and obesity (Excel tables)
facts.table: Table 4: Adults' body mass index (BMI), overweight and obesity prevalence, by age and sex (row '% Obese')
facts.notes: Report text rounds to '29% of adults were living with obesity, and 64% were overweight or living with obesity'.

not_found.why: GP Patient Survey age cross-tabs are only available through its JavaScript analysis tool / national report, which could not be opened from here; HSE 2022 publishes longstanding illness by sex only. Census 2021 any-condition and disability by age (above) used instead.

No official (ONS/NHS) or peer-reviewed nationally representative UK survey of the share of adults who have skipped/stopped prescribed medicine was found; only vendor-commissioned polls (ComRes/Omnicell 2015; Ask Your Pharmacist 2013 among medicine users), not verified or used.

No official or peer-reviewed survey of UK public awareness/knowledge of rare diseases found. Only commercial polls surfaced in search (OnePoll undated; GOSH 2019 online poll: 9% confident naming a childhood rare disease; BIA/YouGov 2021 on access) - none opened at a primary official source, so excluded.
No HRA/NIHR survey of awareness of clinical trials with published method was found; the only participation figure is the weak 2018 NIHR press-release poll recorded above.
APMS 2023/4 'any CMHC' by age (Figure 1.8) is published only as an image; only 16-24, 75+ and 16-64 are stated in text. Not transcribed from the image to avoid estimating.
